titleStmt.title: Huon d'Auvergne, Turin Biblioteca Nazionale Universitaria N III 19 (T) Annotations

div.note: 1] Also transcribed by Holtus (2001), pp. 48-50, lines 1-109; Pasinus, 1-10; Peyron 1-16; Graf (1878) 1-72. Holtus uses a capital at the beginning of each line, and in general gives a diplomatic transcription, not dividing words not divided in the original or in Rajna. We do not note those differences here, only those of different letter transcription. Stengel’s transcription, using Rajna’s copy, also uses capitals at the beginning of the line. His handwriting is much more legible than Rajna’s and he corrects occasional errors, abbreviating “P.R.” for Rajna’s version where needed. Rajna: 1v0 for this first line.

4] Rajna here places a description of the miniature: Min. 1. un re (tutto army) e parecchie altre figure; non intendo bene l'imagin/ Yug. dirige un psonag/ porge un breve/ ad un altro ch 'è/ inginocchiato/ forse l'invito d'uon a corte
5] Numbers in Rajna's notebook are in pencil, added later.Stengel: done e donzele; in margin: d. et d. PR.; Rajna: 2r0 at the beginning of this line.

6] Holtus labels this line as the beginning of 2r. Stengel (Transcription 2b2 T folio 1-2 beginning): En [la] Pentecosta… [el] cavalere novelo, with a note in the margin: [ ] von gleidie… übergeschrieben pentacosta P. R.
7] Rajna: 2r. The manuscript began on a recto when he saw it, with 6 lines: 4 followed by a miniature, with two more following it. Here is the beginning of today's MS.

10] In Rajna's transcription, 'el y.' is inserted above the line with carat below. Note in the right margin of transcription: (corretto l'altro in inchiostro in "o", underlined, refering to novele where the final -e is also underlined. His notes frequently begin with an open parenthesis where there is no close parenthesis. He notes that la is inserted above the line after en before pen. Stengel (Trans. 2b2 T folio 1-2 beginning), writes la in square brackets, with a note at the end of the line and notes at the end of the line that it is written above the line in Rajna, cf. 62/74.
11] Holtus: desirano; Rajna: desi(d)rano, with d inserted above the line. Rajna: 'dire / vevol' (sic) delsoy antesore; could be emended, d'eso= 'that'
12] Stengel: Esteva en…
13] Holtus: mostra cronicha
16] Holtus: folo; no longer visible in MS. Stengel (loc. cit.): En [la] Pentecosta…[el] cavalere novelo, with a note in the margin, “el fehlt bei P. R.”
17] Rajna: un suo servo el caza; Stengel (loc. cit.): el caza, with a note, “el fehlt bei P.R.”, but it is in fact present in Rajna, written as one word with 'caza'.
20] Rajna notes in the margin after belo: (forse "e" i pare sia lett corretta; d’o in e?)
22] Rajna notes "(sic)" after vevole.
23] MS (Rajna): balia, with i inserted above the line; Stengel, Holtus: del relos. "y" crossed out; Rajna: "caratt. più picc / forte aggiunte fatte / poi –i =" (marginal note).
26] MS (Rajna): balia, with i inserted above the line.
31] Stengel: el none yn…; Cf. B 31: Neis la paienie, “Even in pagan lands”; misunderstood; edit, “fino a”31] B 31: Neis la paienie, “Even in pagan lands”; misunderstood; edit, “fino a”
32] Rajna: lobedieno, line before and underneath, line followed by a note: = corr. dache? [corrected from what?]
35] MS (Rajna): balia, with i inserted above the line; Stengel: li meno in ba[i]lia; note in margine, li m. yn b P.R. (correction)
36] Holtus: guernita
37] Holtus: ly bone
39] Stengel: avanzaro; note in margin: avanzare P.R.
40] Holtus marks 2v as beginning here. Holtus: non(n)
41] Stengel: et piu P. R. in the margin; zudeie: not present in the Berlin version: "Jews" (cf. RIALFrI “iudey, Iudei; judei, Judeis,” etc.)
42] Stengel: l’aver e altruy el deserta; in margin, z a. P. R. Rajna appears to read deßta (duplicating the abbreviation for “ser”)
44] gabbo (2) a gabbo, “in segno di scherno, di disprezzo; per burla, per scherzo” (GDLI vol. 6, p. 521, col. 1)

45] Rajna, note in right margin (sic). B 45: Anchois le haete la giant de la contrie. T seems to be missing the verb, "odia"; an emeded reading might be anzo li (odi)a la zente de la contrà. Holtus: Anzo tiera
50] Stengel: ne al ducha ne al valvasore; marginal note: ne a d. ne a v. Rajna’s reading is correct for the portion visible.
59] 59] Stengel: respondino. The MS is damaged in this section with a tear; Rajna: respondeno
63] Rajna note: "prima sao e così / parrebbe ancora / non credo si [atr?] /volz corregg"
66] Rajna reverses these two lines, and uses numbering in the left margin to make clear their order.
68] MS: scratchout after lor and before adobaranse

72] MS: lcomando , with i inserted above the line between l and c; Rajna, note after the line: g. sc. i ( (già scritto i?) Initial E framed; i of quily underlined with correction written above, so unclear which intended, probably initial)
73] Holtus shows the new folio beginning here. Rajna, in the right margin: om for underlines del…peradore, where his writing is scratched over.
76] Cf. Crusca, al dilungo, vol. 1.
79] Rajna, note after chapo: (sotto un’altra parola/ch’molty/ e ra.., che era paltro cefo)
80] Stengel (Transcription, B and T 4-5, etc.): none (for nove)

89] Rajna underlines the final "e", and notes at the end of the line: "e" agg. a .? e così gli altri soto …..?; that final "e" is small, in darker ink, and above the bottom level of the line, though not above the other letters.
90] Stengel (Transcription, B and T 4-5, etc.): Alveregna; Rajna: dal v (with a slash through the middle, up and down)egna. It isn’t clear where or how to apply the abbreviation.
91] Final -"e" here too is different from the other letters of the line.

93] MS (Rajna): Baldovy, with no inserted above the line; Rajna, note "no del solito inchiostro / più nero delle giunte." At the beginning of his transcription, Rajna comments more on the various details of handwriting than in later sections.
96] Rajna: fazone: agg.? with the final -"e" underlined.
97] Rajna: (non g., ma corr.)
98] Final -"e" here too is different.
102] Rajna: seneschalcho, with the first "e" changed into "i" with a dot above and filled in.
104] Rajna: paulo: written above, “corr. in o a.?. (o underlined); in fact, the letter is an -o-, written over another letter.
105] Holtus: de pena trova
107] Holtus: de fin; cf. B 107: Qui forni fu et de fain et d’anons [Which was furnished with both hay and supplies]
109] End of Holtus (2001) transcription.

110] Rajna's notebook has "V" in the left margin, together with a crossed-out label, "IV." Laisse 5, p. 7 of Stengel dossier. He notes at the top: “Nella numerazione (der Blattter von T 9) recente (below the line) ci sono errori; due volte è ripetuto il no 43, e si è saltata la carta che è tra la 91 e la 92 così l’ultimo fo porta il no 129 in luogo del 131.
112] MS (Rajna): zascdun, with a inserted above the line between c and d.
113] MS (Rajna): anpo inserted above the line.
116] MS: zascun, with ad inserted above the line between s and c.
120] Rajna omits this line and later inserts in the right margin, thus beginning the line numbers of his transcription being off from the total.

123] MS (Rajna): ebeute, with u inserted above the line between u and t; Rajna: messy note here, running over beginning of the following line: "O e in? / (non) mi pare" after having crossed out "Em?"; the "non" is written after, squeezed in; he clearly was not sure. The "E" covers the beginning of "Charlo" below.
124] This line omitted in Rajna initially, inserted in right margin according to signal similar to "F." MS: ācorte, at the beginning of the line.

125] prendea: the "e" is not clearly formed, missing the loop. However, here as elsewhere, if there is not a dot for the "i" I presume that it is an "e": thanks to M. Scattolini for this tip. In the right margin, Rajna has added a note, "I vari aggiunti nei margini sono stati saltati nella trascrizione frettolosa." Perhaps this explains the problem with this line: the king should have taken him by the hand, "prenduto" or something similar, and instead there are two verbs, "avè" and "prendea."
156] MS (Rajna): zascun, with ad inserted above the line between s and c.
172] MS: desirano, with d above the line between i and r.
175] yn ponto: ready, prepared (GDLI vol. 14, p. 997, col. 2).

190] MS: fono molte done; There was clearly a saut du même au même here, with “done” repeated one line after the other. B 191: Furent montés por veoir le plus fier [Climbed up high to see who was the fiercest].

194] Rajna: zos, with a mark in the margin; note on left side, referring to that mark: "qui un (a) lett. cancellz/ e sopra scritto un e, a.i./ Si dice legittima, legg. zosa." He has an "a" crossed out in the right margin.
196] MS: baldovĩo; Rajna: baldovij, with a note in the left margin, "corr. in baldovĩo a.i."

199] It is difficult to make sense of this line; I'm interpreting "each of them knocked his own down thoroughly," which requires understanding "le souo" for MS: le sono (the parenthesis are for the emendation). However "n" and "v" are frequently difficult to distinguish; cf. Holtus 1985, p. XXXV.
202] There seems to be a confusion here; it is one person, Berard, both a count and a duke? Cf. B 203: Tot ensemant fu le quisin le dux [So exactly was the duke’s cousin].
206] Rajna initially misses this line and inserts it afterward in the margin.
207] MS: logamente
209] MS: MS: el bon Artus: les bornes Artu, the limits of the known world, Roman d’Alexandre.
212] MS (Rajna): non aza, with n inserted above the line between the two groups.

219] There are a couple of ways that this could be interpreted: first, "le roi... / armé, et avec toutes ses armes décorées d'une fleur de lys"; or, "[the king] is armed in weapons all decorated with a fleur-de-lys"; that is, the second word of the line could be a verb or the conjunction.

221] elziso: this form seems to be from alzire/elzire; cf. Aquilon de Bavière, "to kill"; the line then means, "that is, Huon, who wouldn't have killed him [Berardo] at all." Compare to B, where the verb is "to hate."
240] This line does not make sense, since the copyist didn't understand the type of horse, "amoravis" and changed the term to something he knew! Compare with B.
243] Rajna's copy shows a spot above "quelo," but it does not seem to be a dot to an "i" merely an imperfection in the paper.

246] Illumination follows: Rajna, "2 giostra." In fact there is a view of one horsed man from the front, with a crown on his head and a sun on his chest in the center of the page; behind, to the right, there is a side view of a figure in grey on horseback with his lance at the attack position, with the same sun motif on the horse's caparison and a cape visible on his back. Sofrise = ‘interceded’; cf. T-L sofrage
249] MS: vivo; cf. B 250: Bien soit de voir tant cum il fust vestis [Yet he knew well that as long as he wore]
263] Rajna initially omits this line and adds it in the margin afterwards.
302] B: selong lor coi[n]tenance. Nowhere else in this MS does any such form "sealonga" appear.
306] Rajna initially skips this line and adds it later in the left margin.
313] Rajna note: "li lom o loim, non /loin; ma / il segno sopra non / è un i troppo/ legittimo, ma rro/ poi (mi pare) un segno / p l'asta sotta / posta – se è / fu mal fatto."
325] MS (Rajna): possa presso, with a inserted above the line before the second group.
330] Rajna, note in margin: (sir, voglio)
356] "a dove a dove"= a due a due; cf. "sove" = sue
363] This line and the following are initially incorrectly ordered in Rajna, who then writes numbers in the left margin to indicate the correct order.

380] MS (Rajna): sono sorprisse, with el inserted above the line between the two groups; sorprisse: there is a dot above the second "r," not above the following vowel; Rajna has a note, ‘da chi? forse /corr =y; ai/ [for the final -e] corr. da o’; Stengel (Transcription 13 B and T laisses 14-15): sorpresse.
413] Rajna notes that he is not sure whether the MS reads "in" or "m." The strokes are linked.

417] Illumination: two men under tree, one with horns and bells, , the other with hat over his eyes; one figure has his arm around the tree; the figure beside him wears a giant turban-like hat; short skirt and long puffy sleeves; both face right. Rajna: “Figura (il re trasfigury. guarda le donne uscire e passare)”.
418] The MS has been scratched: ve:y is what the MS looks like. B: Quant vos forma (l. 421)
434] MS: non sia y[n] tal locho metuto; we omit the negative since it does not make sense here. Cf. B 437, Que vetre amors seit en tiel leu basti [To place your love in such a situation]
436] Rajna has a mark after "chy" and before "ßve" that is unclear; it looks like a little caret. Perhaps this should read "ss[er]ve"?
438] Rajna omits the "o" of "yo."
440] There seems to be a line missing here; cf. B 444: Non ai ge soingn fors tout soul de celli [I have no desire except for the one] (between this line and the following).
443] Rajna omits the "u" of "nuy." These two omissions make one wonder about the "y" in line 444—should it be "yo"?
451] MS: yo aza la segnoria [that I have lordship]; B 455: Mes Amor veut qui ait la segnorie [But Love wants to have lordship]; it doesn’t make sense that Charles rule over lovers.

458] Rajna: dona chre. da more al quanto asentire; Stengel (Transcription, 17): Dona chi è d’amore alquanto asentire; B 462: qui ni ert d'amors auque asentie [A lady who has never accepted love even a little]
459] Rajna transcribes in reverse order this and the following line; he numbers in left margin to indicate the need to reorder. B 463: la monte d’une lie: [the amount of a fig]
463] Rajna: ne piga. He underlines the word and has a line under the "p"; would seem to have been uncertain himself of the reading. B 467: emplie.
476] Cf. Dante and the pilgrim's expressions of shame: e.g., Inf. 17.85-90.
478] For "se tene y[n]tra ello" B 482: si tient traie
480] MS: retona, with r above the line between o and n; MS (Rajna): sede partia, with s above the line after the first group.
484] After the second "pensery," Rajna notes (sic).
485] Rajna: anyda parla
491] Possible misapprehension of an original form of OF haer, using here avere; cf. B 495: E conuit bien que la giant luy haoit [He also knew very well that the people hated him].
495] MS: vora, with i inserted above the line between r and a.
506] MS: convira, with i inserted above the line between r and a.
514] MS: sorprende, with e inserted above the line between r and p; Rajna initially omits this line, then inserts it in the left margin.
520] Rajna has a number of marks above this line that appear to be abbreviations: "razŷ...tōrmenta."
525] Rajna initially omits this line, then inserts it in the left margin.
528] studevelmente: ‘deliberately, in an intentional manner’ (GDLI vol. 7, p. 419, col. 3).
529] MS: baron nano, with nō inserted before nano.
544] B 549: Ja estes sire, et tot a vos atent [You are the ruler and everything depends on you].
552] MS: ve lamenta enō, with de inserted above the line after ta.
554] MS: pensero coro, with e inserted above the line between the two groups of letters.
563] MS (Rajna): ambasa enovele, with te inserted above the line between the two grouups of letters.
569] The second half of this line is problematic; the hemistich reads in B 574: 'Oïl, mon bon segnor'.
572] bosadro: cf. AdB buxarde, ‘menteur’; TLIO, ‘bugiadro’ [liar]

574] The original was misunderstood here: B 579: “Des or, entant a moy” [Now, listen to me]: “desor” as one word would be ‘above’, which, as here, does not make sense. This continues to line 577, the equivalent of which in B 582 reads ‘Des or en avant’ [From here on out, from here henceforth].
583] Cf. B 588: Mes autre ni puit estre, grand desirer nen n’oy! [But I can’t change how I feel; I’ve never had such a great desire!]
621] MS (Rajna): Ɔfia, with d inserted above the line between i and a.

623] savye: where the ink is worn, it is frequently difficult to see the tail below the line; this could well read savie. However, under the light the tail can be seen. Here the tail is only visible with the ultraviolet light.
624] Rajna reverses this line and the following, noting the correct order in the left margin.
tratuty: archaic, trattutto (2), pl. ‘everyone without exclusion’ (GDLI vo. 29, p. 269, col. 2).
652] Rajna reads "guer" but the MS clearly reads a sapiate just at the edge of the burned portion.
669] Illumination follows (Rajna: "4 Fig (Carlo e Sandino).
670] MS: nuy; Rajna: vuy; MS (Rajna): anun ȳnoia, with e inserted above the line after the first n.
675] yndusia: MSI indugio, ‘hesitation, delay, lingering’
680] Rajna, marginal note: "e dei corr. Sng."; this last must be an abbreviation.
683] MS (Rajna): respeto etardare, with n inserted above the line between the two groups of letters.
686] "Si non, défiez le..." (Literally, "Cela si il se trouve [si il est] que non)"

691] Cf. B 696: Tant savreç d’engin et des art plus de lor [You would know the tricks and arts better than [the Devil]]. Notice the incomprehension of ‘d’engin’ and the use of ‘sentirsi’ instead of ‘sapere’.
693] MS: remoure el, with e inserted above the line after u.
700] MS: prendra, with e inserted above the line between d and r.
714] Rajna omits initially and then inserts in the left margin.

715] "vezo" seems to be an error for “voio” o “voro”; Rajna has edited his initial letters so that they are more difficult to read than usual, but the “z” is clear. Perhaps a misreading by a scribe for an above the line “z”, which does appear elsewhere in the text.
729] Rajna reverses this line and the following, and indicates the correct order by numbering in the left margin.
743] Both appearances of the terme 'requilie' show reciprocal metathesis for reliquie. See v. 751 below.

750] End of the first fascicle of Rajna's notebook. Second begins with next line, "Tor. 2." in upper corner, with "13" in red underneath. From here on, there are only numbers in red in the upper right corner of each opening, not sequential numbers as in the first fascicle.

756] in rimando: cf. di rimando: ‘con una risposta pronta anche mordace, appropriata per ribattere alle parole dell’interlocutore’ [with a quick and even biting answer, appropriate to respond to the interlocutor] (GDLI vol. 16, p. 383, col. 3).

758] viva: these last four letters are distinctly different from the other strokes around them. They are smaller, and written above the bottom line of the rest of the verse. Added afterwards, with a different pen? Perhaps originally the end read "li à"?

762] Before "aƣpir" there is a little stroke above the line. However, since there is no caret or other mark to indicate insertion, I do not include it in the text. Rajna: apreso; MS clear has "apresso."
765] Cf. B 771: Por li pecaor ert feit quant l’arme spitera [For the sinner it happens when its soul exits (the body)]
770] MS (Rajna): fa (te) Charlo; Rajna note: te altro inch[iostro]; B 776: “Hé,” feit li rois, “bon quuens, et qi dites vos ja? [“Oh,” said the king, “my good count, what are you saying? […]].
776] The section from lines 774-76 has ink transfer from the illumination that blocks out sections of text.
777] MS: a ntendre za, with i and a second e above the line. Rajna notes, ‘la 2a corr[ezione] d’altro inch[iostro] che la prima’.

783] MS (Rajna): nuy; B 789: Si nuls ja por soe force del mien me tenira [Whether anyone will, by his own power, keep any part of what belongs to me]. As it stands, the line makes no sense, so we emend to follow B.

786] Illumination follows this line. Huon is kneeling before a double-crowned figure on a what seems to be a tiled floor (alternating dark and light), looking at a book that figure is holding open. Other figures are visible to the right, and one stands on the side of Huon, a little to our left looking at a book. Rajna leaves a bit of a blank but does not summarize the illumination as he later does; he does write “Giura”..

799] See B 804-805: "Sens, abstinance, proece, tot ingual / In vos habite et ont pris son hostal." The Turin version is missing a line, "Intelligence, abstinence, ability, all equally..." or something similar, before this line.
803] MS (Rajna): baron cosy, with tuto inserted above the line between the two letter groups.
809] MS: credre, with e inserted above the line after d. Rajna reverses this and the next line, and numbers in the left margin to indicate the correct order.
813] pi(ù): blot on page at this point: cannot read the letter underneath.
820] As Scattolini notes, vv. 820-821 are reversed in order in comparison with B, creating difficulties in meaning. We reverse them here.
822] MS: credre, with e inserted above the line after d.
823] Rajna notes "altro inch[iostro]/.d. /e mano"; the remaining MS text does not show notable differences, so he must be referring to the initial. The reference for the ".d." is unclear.

824] Cf. B 830: Conse inposible quier, bien le puis coneoir [I am seeking something impossible, I know it well]; it would seem that ‘quier’ was not understood. “domandate” might be a reasonable emendation here.
825] Rajna initially omits this line, then inserts it in the left margin.
829] MS (Rajna): prendrazo, with e inserted above the line after d.
838] MS: ȳmperore, with ad inserted before the final -ore. Again, Rajna notes in the margin this change in another ink.

841] MS (Rajna): lomperore, with ad inserted before the final -ore. Rajna transcribes ‘lomperer’ and in the note in the margin, writes ‘corr. in lomperadore’. Stengel (Transcription 38 B and T 839ff) does not note emendations separately, he includes them in his transcription. Since the first is visible in the original MS and precedes the second by a few lines only, and because it follows the pattern of reinsertion of syncopes, it is included here.
844] The capital is like a "G" in capital form in Rajna.
846] MS (Rajna): ȳ teramente, with g inserted above the line between e and r.

854] Rajna has a large ink blot at the beginning of (his) 845-46 that blocks part of the reading, and at the end of his 846, has some difficulties: unclear if "fassemo" and then corrects to "demora" (the "o" has been changed and reinforced).
856] MS: tā crossed out after zuro.

859] MS: parlo eposa, with no inserted above the line after parlo. The MS currently seems to have a dot on the line after parlo as if to transform the final vowel into -a, but whether it is an afterthought or just a spot is unclear.
863] Before che: crossed out word
864] ell'era = "ello era"
870] MS (Rajna): mtre, with e inserted above the line after m.
874] asentite: assentito, ‘cautious, prudent’ (GDLI vol 1, p. 758).
902] MS (Rajna): afare de lo conte (with “de” above the line, inserted; it seems to be inserted in an incorrect position, either by Rajna or by the scribe).
906] MS (Rajna): corte renputa, with e inserted above the line between the two groups of letters.
913] Rajna omits this line initially and inserts it later in the right margin.
919] MS: che la zente de la tera et àno veduto un zopo; Cf. B 926: Que la giant de la terre ad aute vos huçoit [The local people called out in loud voices]; we omit “et” for sense.
940] B: mot for “molto” here; however, “moto” for ‘word’ is not unknown here, with more than 30 appearances, so it seems to be an error.

942] Illumination follows this line. Much of the color is gone: to the far right a ruler under a baldicchino throne wearing a hat with two levels (the upper recessed in relation to the lower) sits while a male figure in parti-colored tights to the viewer's left with his back to the reader holds something in his arms; another figure further to the reader's left is partially visible. Rajna: Due scene in un solo quadro (e paesaggio)- sotto: Ug domanda al fante d’and- / sopra: il donzello che tira pei suo cappelli; e percuote il pelleg.), so we are missing half of the illumination.
952] hoze: oggi. Cf. vv. 6426, 10459 (oze)
963] pane buffetto (3): ‘tipo di pane soffice e leggero’ [type of soft and light bread’ (GDLI vol. 2, p. 430).
964] Rajna: piuue? piude? piuie? B: cu[n] estre puisent plu. The final strokes of Rajna's handwritten copy are not clear.
973] MS: fustue?

982] Illumination follows. Rajna: "Figura. "La e più bella d'assai fin qui trovata è doppia con una sola scena / a destro il palazzo con due torri, dall'uscio si vede nel portony Ugo/ benedire le vivande della tavola a cui siede il pilgri_ a sinistra/ si vede in alto un diavolo che vola colla tavola, e sotto fuori dall'uscio/ Ugo e altri che guardon su con atti di meraviglia _ una donna sta / meraviglij o piuttosto atterita a una finestra _ c'è espressione
983] B 990: Se cil Sire non panse qui tu adores plu [If that Lord whom you love so much doesn’t take care of you]
992] Rajna seems to have "lafu" crossed out before the final "lafu," whether correcting his own error or one of the MS is unclear.
1001] MS: lize, with di inserted above the line after li.
1012] tratutto: ‘tutto, tutto quanto’ [everything, the whole thing]; tratutti: ‘tutti senza esclusione’ [everyone, without exception] (GDLI vol. 21, p. 269, column 2).

1015] m’astanio: there is no verb *astaniare or *staniare in the GDLI. stanare: ‘3. Trovare con qualche difficoltà un oggetto nascosto o poco visibile [to find something hidden or hard to see with difficulty]; 4. Fig. ‘Individuare o accertare ciò che non risulta evidente’ [to identify or verify what is not immediately clear] (GDLI vol 10, pp. 67-68).
1024] à maistrà: it is unclear whether this is present or past; both ammaestrare and maestrare appear in Old Italian (OVI).

In B vv. 3147 and 3149, the count climbs the hill and rests on his way up it; tertre for ‘hill’ seems to pose a comprehension/translation problem.

4016] ingreso: cf. GdA, “avido; appassionato; fiero, orgoglioso”; Holtus, Lexikalische, “terrible” (pp. 350-51). This may be a combination of Italian “ingresso” ((1) masculine noun, 'spazio attraverso cui si accede ad un ambiente; principio, esordio; facoltà di entrare in un luogo' attested fourteenth century, TLIO) and the OF that also appears in Italian ((2) adjective 'impetuoso e ostile; crudele; oltracotante' attested thirteenth century, TLIO). The T construction would suggest a noun in Italian, so the first alternative; however, the 'syntagme nominal' construction in French might allow for the second usage (exhibited in Modern French by 'drôle de guerre'). Cf. B 4137: l ’engres du lionoit'

Rajna, in right margin: "corr. non s'intende/ da che" (lo traditore). The sense here is that Saudin does not approve (or pretends to not approve) of those who had an aggressive or too rigid attitude. In Berlin, ll. 5308-15, the reading differs. The messengers and Ynide's men went out to eat and drink together, and Carlo Martello's men and Ynide's divided up into groups in which the messengers attempt to persuade Ynide's men to help them. (line 5097 = Saudin and Thomais; 5125 = Ruger and Baldovyn; 5126 = the archbishop and Berard "le çatan", the captain. Here is repeated at 5127 Berardo with Morando and Ynrigo, missing from B.There was clearly a miscomprehension somewhere along the line of this text: B reads "Berart the captain"; either our scribe here or an earlier one in this text's line understood "Satan" instead of "captain," which alters the meaning.

8636] Antenor was, in OF tradition, a traitor; a Trojan, and advisor to King Priam of Troy, in Classical tradition he advised the Trojans to return Helen and encouraged negotiations with the Greeks. 8843] vera: ‘bolt’ or ‘quarrel’; Italian for verreton, a large bolt. And it would appropriately fly very quickly from a crossbow. Many thanks to Kelly DeVries for this information. (27 June, 2017, personal email). tranzise: from transire, ‘to pass through’; cf. AdB tranze, tranzés (RIALFrI, 19 April 2026).

9800] Renier, p. 52; "Death by chessboard" is a chanson de geste motif: in the Geste Francor, Ogier the Dane kills Charlot, Charlemagne's son, with a chessboard; in Renaut de Montauban, Bertholet has died thus also, and further incidents appear in the Batârd de Bouillon and in Parise la duchesse, but there is no known incident relating to Thibaut killing his brother-in-law Folco in the East. On chess in the Middle Ages and its uses, see Jenny Adams, Power Play: The Literature and Politics of Chess in the Late Middle Ages (U of Penn P, 2006); Nicholas Perkins, ed., Medieval Romance and Medieval Culture (D. S. Brewer, 2015). An Italian novella, in fact, insists on Thibaut's family relationship to Guillaume through Folco (married to Anfelise, Thibaut's stepsister, niece of Desramé), I Conti di antichi cavalieri, ed. Alberto del Monte (Cisalpino-Goliardica, 1972), 118-22.

9988] This scene may refer to the beginning of the mass; at that era, the "introit involves the singing of a Psalm, which by this period would have been sung alternatingly by two choir bodies," and that might account for the "a bis" idea. Alternatively, it may be like improvisory practice where "one singer or group of singers would sing the original chant tune, and the other voices might improvise or sing composed counterpoint above it" and "vocal polyphony was used during mass, often with a low line carrying the chant tune, and upper voices providing countermelodies, improvised or otherwise." Where and when it was done and if the celebrant was involved would be difficult to verify since the specific origin of this story is not known. We thank Remi Chiu, Assoc. Prof. of Fine Arts (Music) at LUM for his collaboration. Rajna appears to read "sovrananza" but the MS is clear.

10026] MS: coro. These two lines are seriously miscontrued- it is necessary to read Berlin to have any idea of the meaning, which seems to be something like "He who is in that place will have a good night and day; / those who wait for it, guilty, [I believe] that it will go badly for them." Berlin 10374 reads "Qui l'attend, cro je, mout li stara mal". If this MS reads "attend rio coro", it may have been "attendrio c¯do" with an abbreviation line over the "c" and a long upper stroke over the "d", or something similar ("e"'s and "o"'s are frequently difficult to distinguish and if the upper stroke of the "d" were long, running into the abbreviation mark, there could seem to be two "o'"s with an abbreviation mark for an "r"). Or, if the reading is "iuro" – instead of "coro"—then "I swear".... In any case, it seems to be an expression of opinion on the part of the speaker.

10046] falcon da rivera: it is unclear what this means specifically; it may be an osprey, aka river hawk or sea hawk, or it may be a falcon trained to hunt by a river. Ospreys actually submerge into the water, while peregrines are known for their speed of diving and rapid descent. De scientia venandi per aves, a translation into Latin from Arabic, circulated widely and was known in northern Italy through Daniel Deloc da Cremona (see Le Livre de Moamin; Livers des oisseax et des bestes de rapine (1249-1272), Serena Modena, https://www.rialfri.eu/en/opere/le-livre-de-moamin, consulted 7 May 2026).

MS, Rajna: che lavea; B 11991: Que aige merci de la giant que la voit [That He have mercy on the people whom He saw there]. Here, there are several possibilities: ch'el avea [that he had]; che l'avea [that had him]; or che là veaex [whom he saw there]. There are no other appearances of "vea" for the verb 'to see', but there are more than 200 of "avea" from 'to have', so I have chosen that while recognizing the other possibilities.

11627] The print is much smaller in this line, though still the same forms of letters. Rajna underlines mostrate at the beginning of the line and repeats it at the end in the margin; the MS does read "mostrate" at the end of the line; it's unclear whether it is there for a specific reason, so we do not repeat it.

11633] There are two possible interpretations here: either "s[er]vize" is a verb (MSI servisse) or a noun (MSI servizio). Either "God orders that you be in his service always, without sin until now, now in the future [litt., straight ahead]" or "God orders that you serve him now; you are without sin so far up to now" (this second line would parallel Berlin). "s[er]vize" is problematic, it is a hapaxlegomenon. "servisio" appears 9 times, "serviso" 1 time, "servigio" one time, together with various forms of the verb "servir(e)"; the –ize ending appears primarily in "dize" (490 times, = MSI disse) but also in "lize" = legge; "genetrize", "meretrize" = genetrice, meretrice; "fize" = fece; "amize" = amici (5 times); "radize" = radici (9 times); and in the name "Galudize". Thus either interpretation can be defended: like disse or like servizio. If the verb is the chosen interpretation, the punctuation differs: after "tutora" would be a semicolon, with nothing after "tu sey" in the following line.

I. 14 (Cod. 89) from 188-190; this is a resumé of Octavian. From folio 190V-192V, he speaks of Cod. xxvj =L. II.14 (?) of parchment sec. XIIIo o XIVo 586 folios in 2 columns, with a listing of contents, including Bovo d'Antona.
